metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent used Find & Replace with format conditions to change all 21 italic runs from 12pt to 14pt in Y22-2119-assign4.docx, then saved with Ctrl+S. Task completed in 15 turns with score 1.0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Find & Replace, set font format conditions (italic style, size), use Replace All, and save documents.
metadata.explanation: Variation with a different target size (16pt instead of 14pt). Getter checks all 21 italic runs are 16pt. Initial state has all italic runs at 12pt (fails). The model must apply the same Find & Replace technique but with 16pt as the replacement size.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets the right file (Y22-2119-assign4.docx), right formatting property (italic runs), and right size value (16pt), semantically aligned with the instruction.
Metric correctly validates: checks for dict result without error, confirms all_italic_size_16 is True, and ensures italic_count > 0 to prevent trivial pass on empty document.
Metric does not access expected parameter incorrectly — it relies entirely on the getter result dict, avoiding the rule-parameter bug.
Postconfig includes Ctrl+S and 2-second sleep to ensure the file is saved before the getter fetches it from the environment.

Minor coverage gap: getter only iterates doc.paragraphs and misses italic runs inside table cells. If the document contains italic text in tables, those runs will be silently skipped, potentially causing false positives or false negatives.

run.italic returns None for inherited italic (from paragraph/style), not True; such runs would be missed by the getter. However, after a Find & Replace operation that explicitly sets italic formatting, this is unlikely to cause issues in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Extend the getter to also iterate table cells: for table in doc.tables: for row in table.rows: for cell in row.cells: for para in cell.paragraphs: for run in para.runs: ...
Consider whether runs with run.italic == None should be included using the effective italic value from the paragraph or style, to catch style-inherited italic formatting.
